title: Priority Scoring Formula for Enterprise Compliance Requests (use-case + data-paths)
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a deterministic priority-scoring formula for incoming enterprise security & compliance asks (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires). The goal is to replace ad-hoc human routing with an explainable score that drives SLA lane assignment, initial resource allocation, and evidence-bundling templates.

Why this matters:
- Current triage is slow and inconsistent; enterprise deals stall while answers are being routed and evidence collected.
- A repeatable scoring model will reduce time-to-first-response, standardize SLAs, and enable partial automation for low-risk asks.

Proposed approach (two parts):
1) Minimal intake form (fast-path): capture use-case, data types, region(s), vendor/third-party exposure, requested standard (SOC2/HIPAA/etc.), and legal ask type (DPA, RFI, questionnaire). Also capture estimated customer tier and potential revenue impact.
2) Scoring formula: compute base score as weighted sum of: data sensitivity (0-10), regulatory scope multiplier (1.0-2.5), cross-border data flow flag (+3), business impact bucket (0-8), number of controls requested (0-5 normalized). Apply heuristics: automatic escalation if data sensitivity >=8 OR business impact >=7 OR control_count >=20. Final score maps to lanes: 0-9 low (async self-serve), 10-17 medium (PM+Solutions), 18+ high (Sales+Legal+Security immediate).

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake UI/endpoint captures required fields and persists to intake DB.
- Scoring endpoint returns numeric score and lane label; score explanation returned as structured text (explainability required).
- SLA estimator panel predicts expected TTR (time-to-response) per lane and shows expected assignee team.
- Evidence templates selected automatically based on detected standard(s) and data-paths.
- Telemetry: distribution of scores, time-to-first-response by lane, and false-positives/negatives flagged in review.

Open design decisions / trade-offs:
- Weighting values: initially tuned from historical dataset of ~320 closed compliance asks; may require manual calibration. Trade-off between sensitivity (catch all) vs noise (over-escalation).
- Explainability format: lightweight bullet list vs structured JSON. Start with bullet list for Console display, keep structured JSON for API consumers.
- Ownership for ongoing calibration: propose Security/PM guild shared responsibility with quarterly review.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (internal alpha): expose API + internal UI, route to a human-in-loop triage queue (no automatic escalations). Measure precision/recall. (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta): enable automatic lane assignment with conservative thresholds, enable evidence template suggestions. (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (GA): fully automated routing, SLA notifications, and dashboards. (after 6 weeks, subject to calibration)

Metrics to monitor:
- % asks auto-assigned vs manual override
- avg time-to-first-response by lane
- number of escalations reversed by humans
- conversion lift for deals once SLA lowered

Implementation notes for Eng:
- New API: POST /intake/v1/score returning {score:int, lane:string, reasons:list} (console will display reasons as text).
- Persist both raw inputs and the computed explanation in intake table for auditability.
- Provide an admin calibration UI to tweak weights without deploys.
- Connect to evidence storage to auto-suggest doc bundles (SOC2 evidence pack, DPA clauses, HIPAA controls mapping).

Links to artifacts and drafts:
- Intake mockups: https://confluence.redwood.in/display/PM/Compliance+Intake+Scoring+Mocks
- Historical dataset (internal): https://drive.redwood.in/pm/compliance/historical-asks-2023-2026.csv
- Initial scoring notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-scoring/blob/main/notebooks/initial_weights.ipynb

Risks and mitigations:
- Over-escalation may overload Security: start conservative and instrument overrides.
- Mis-classification of jurisdiction: require explicit user confirmation for cross-border flows.

Next steps:
- Review proposal with Security (action: security review scheduled 2026-03-12).
- Engineering spike: build minimal scoring endpoint and Wire up to internal triage queue (owner: ENG-4910).
- Design finalize microcopy for explainability in intake form (owner: Design).
